speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I have three supplementary questions for the Minister of State.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: First on part (a), which is a general question on Immigration and Checkpoints Authority's (ICA's) policy with regard to deportation of foreigners convicted in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: From my past experience, it is quite normal for foreigners to be sent back to their home countries.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: For example, if you are a Malaysian, you will be deported to Malaysia; if you are an Indonesian, likewise, and so on.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The second supplementary question is that, on this recent money laundering case, out of the seven who had been deported to Cambodia so far, at least three of them do not seem to be holding Cambodian passports.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: That is based on the information which I could glean publicly.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: That means out of the seven deported to Cambodia, three of them do not seem to be holding Cambodian passports.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: So, I wonder if the Ministry can explain the choice, why they were deported to Cambodia, for those who are not Cambodian nationals.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The third question, out of the 10 arrested in this recent case, five were reported to be wanted by China and they are holding Chinese passports.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: So, my question is, why are they not being returned to China?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: First and foremost, to start off with, the examples that she shared about previous instances could be a case whereby the subject did not hold multiple passports.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: And therefore, the only country in which the subject could be deported to, was the subject's home country.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: In this case, the 10 subjects hold multiple passports.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: On the second question that she had, about three of them not holding Cambodian passports, I am not aware of this situation.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I would find that quite odd, because when we undertake deportation processes, we would look at whether or not they are admissible to the country of their choice.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: And that would include whether or not they hold a passport that allows them to enter the country.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The third and last question the Member had was why they were not deported back to China, right?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: As I mentioned earlier, the foreigners can go to any country which their passport or travel document allows them to go.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, for these 10 subjects, they had chosen to be deported to Cambodia or Japan, at least for these 10 subjects.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: First is, my analysis of who held what passports are based on the publicly available reports.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: So, based on what I have discerned, there are three of them being deported to Cambodia who are not Cambodian national – so, Ministry can contradict me if I am wrong in what I found.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: So, is she saying that the offenders have a right to indicate which jurisdiction they would like to be deported to?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Because she used the word "chose", so, I would like the Minister of State to clarify that.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Last of all, my understanding is that there is an extradition treaty between Cambodia and China.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: So, I wonder whether she can or cannot confirm whether this was one of the factors taken into account in deporting seven of these offenders to Cambodia.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I have shared what I understood about this matter in my earlier reply.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Sorry, could I get the Member to repeat her last point again, please?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: The second one was about the fact that the Minister of State mentioned that these offenders chose to go to Cambodia or Japan.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: So, my question is, do offenders have the right to choose which country they would like to be deported to?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: So, if I decide that I want to go very far away to Canada, can I just say that, even if I have no connection with that country?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: So, anyway, specifically on that case, whether they had the right to choose?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: And last of all, was the question of the existence of an extradition treaty between China and Cambodia, and whether that was one of the considerations which led to the Government deporting seven of these offenders to Cambodia.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I think what is important is that where subjects hold multiple passports, there is an assessment by the Ministry, as to whether or not they are admissible to the country based on the travel documents that they have.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We make that assessment and then we successfully deport them.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Last clarification, again on the issue of choice.
